question: In an early build of your support agent, the agent reads order data through a generic run_backend_query tool that accepts any SQL statement. Production logs show that when a customer gives a mistyped order number, the agent sometimes reads and quotes an order that belongs to a different customer. Your team wants the tool interface itself to block such lookups. Which change best achieves this?

options.text: Keep run_backend_query and add few-shot examples to the system prompt that show the agent writing queries filtered by the current customer's ID.
options.reason: Few-shot examples only guide the model's behavior; the unconstrained tool still accepts queries for other customers' orders.

options.text: Keep run_backend_query and force tool_choice to get_customer on the first turn, so that the agent always identifies the customer before it runs any query.
options.reason: Forced tool selection only fixes the order of calls; the generic query tool can still read any customer's order afterward.

options.text: Keep run_backend_query and greatly lengthen its description with the full table schema and column meanings, so that the agent writes more precise SQL statements for each order lookup it performs.
options.reason: A richer description may improve query accuracy, but the tool remains generic and still lets a mistyped order number return another customer's data.

options.text: Replace run_backend_query with a lookup_order tool that takes an order ID and the verified customer ID, and that rejects orders owned by another account with an error.
options.reason: Replacing a generic tool with a constrained alternative that validates its input makes the interface itself refuse lookups outside the customer's account.
